**The document doesn't give these numbers.** The TL;DR win-rate plot (Figure 2, right) is embedded as an image (`tldr_winrate_vs_temp.svg`), so I can't read the plotted values for PPO or DPO at temperature 1.0. I also can't give page numbers, because this HTML version has no page markers. I've cited sections and figures instead.

What the text does say about high temperatures:

- **PPO:** DPO is "much more robust to the sampling temperature than PPO, the performance of which can degrade to that of the base GPT-J model at high temperatures" (Section 6.2). The caption of Figure 2 also says DPO is "more robust to changes in the sampling temperature."
- **PPO at 1.0 specifically:** In the human study, PPO at temperature 1.0 is called the "lowest" performing setting (Section 6.4). Table 2 gives PPO-1 win rates of 13% (GPT-4 S), 12% (GPT-4 C) and 17% (humans). These numbers are not the plot values you asked about: they compare PPO at 1.0 against PPO at temperature 0, while the plot compares against human-written reference summaries.
- **Only exact plot-related numbers:** DPO is about 61% at temperature 0.0, and PPO is about 57% at its best temperature, also 0.0 (Section 6.2).

To get the exact values at 1.0, you'd need the figure itself or the PDF version of the paper.
